answers.answer: Roll one die for each held office card and add one for each fatigue on that card; the Chairman also adds one. A modified 1–2 has no effect, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the officeholder. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: ‘Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a display card. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending. Ties go to the player with the most total windows, including newly acquired prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. There is no immediate replacement; after the selection step discard all remaining cards and refill the display with exactly three cards—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody took one. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige: ‘Players who retired at least one pensioner’ act in ‘descending actual total retirement spending’; ties use ‘most total windows’ then clockwise from PM.

answers.answer: Each player takes one chosen family action and puts their opportunity marker on it. If the marker was already on that action at phase start, the player may take the action twice; the marker starts off the board. If laws grant extra actions, only the latest passed extra-action law can be used; that extra action is not doubled by the marker and does not move it. With at least four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once that turn. Thus if the marker already sits on Enlist Writer, it can be used twice, and with four vacant offices each use gets the one-time additional writer: three writers total, not four.
answers.evidence: Family: a marker already on the action permits it ‘twice’; extra-action law action ‘receives no opportunity-marker doubling.’ Enlist Writer: with at least four vacant offices, one additional writer ‘once this turn,’ so a doubled action can place three total.

answers.answer: After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both applicants and Debt remain. If Debt is gone, slide the remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Money paid to seek a share is paid to the bank; it is not paid into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: New Company shares: ‘move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one’; with no Debt, applicants slide right. ‘Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.’

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on the backs of their cards. Ordinary own-family hiring requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. When promoting an officeholder, transfer the old officeholder’s fatigue to the new card and put the old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate, or the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ‘Fill vacant offices in ascending number’; own-family hiring requires consent of ‘every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool’; promotion transfers fatigue and inserts the old card vacant.

answers.answer: The former Chairman announces a candidate with a pure majority of current shares, meaning more than half. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. If no candidate gets majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The winner’s Company share is moved into the Chairman slot and still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but it cannot be traded or invested in firms.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: ‘pure majority of current shares (more than half)’; if no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder. Chairman-slot share ‘cannot be traded or invested in firms.’

answers.answer: For a Company-office check, first commit resources and pay any required cash from that acting office’s treasury to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue, and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Success checks: Company-office check cash comes from ‘that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank’; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 failure/retry, 5–6 catastrophe and officeholder/card destinations.

answers.answer: The Chairman may add up to three Debt without consent, adding £5 to Balance for each advance. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, with the Chairman counting toward that majority; never advance past the Debt track end. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer, and may interleave borrowing and allocation as long as the borrowing limits are respected. Cash already in office treasuries remains there for those offices to use.
answers.evidence: Chairman: ‘add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance’; additional advance requires majority-share consent; ‘Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries.’

answers.answer: Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Each acquired ship may be placed in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Leased extra ships serve only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping: ‘Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains’; costs and conditions listed for extra, fitted, and Company ships.

answers.answer: The President declares regions for Trade, including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys one die, and subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failure can be retried during the President’s uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; another position cannot act between attempts. Catastrophe removes the President. The President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions. The first writer goes to the home port; each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another President’s home region even if that office is vacant. Increase Company Balance by each order’s printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under deregulation. The President gets £1 from the bank per order, and writer owners get £1 per writer placed.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: declaration, £1-per-die and nonhome penalty, retry and catastrophe rules, one successful Trade, route/writer rules, protected home regions, Balance and bonuses.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their Presidency’s home region, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency’s home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhausted officers and regiments each produce one die; local alliances contribute their printed dice. Subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. A noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy steps 1–3: target limits; dice from exhausted pieces and alliances; empire-strength penalty; losses checked ‘after each attempt.’

answers.answer: On a successful Deploy, the loot pool is £4 per tower in the target plus the faceup loot-token modifier, with a minimum of one pound plus the number of surviving officers used. Distribute one £1 share to the Commander and one per surviving used officer belonging to the Commander; give £1 clockwise for each other player’s surviving used officer; then pay £1 to the bank per regiment and per alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength. Repeat the distribution cycle until the loot is gone. The Commander gains one trophy per target tower. For control, remove the tower and dome, and if the target was a capital remove all matching empire flags; open all its orders and clear unrest. If the region becomes Company-controlled, place its loot/control token region-side above the President, and place a Governor overlay and office card in vacancies. If the Elephant was in the conquered region and pointing outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and their member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and there is no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: success lists loot formula, distribution, trophies and control changes; catastrophe states trophy return and Commander destination.

answers.answer: A Governor starts with the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without a penalty, then reduces the pool by one. A success pays the Governor £1, plus another £1 if the previous roll was unsuccessful, and allows one choice: build a Company ship (first success places a partially built ship in the region; a later successful Build completes it into the associated President’s sea zone), commission a regiment into that President’s Army, or Tax by adding £2 unsplit to Balance or the President’s treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Every unsuccessful check adds unrest. The Governor may continue until choosing to stop, running out of dice, or rolling catastrophe; catastrophe follows normal office removal.
answers.evidence: Governors: Administer: printed pool decreases after each roll; success pay and choices, additional Tax unrest, failed-check unrest, and stop/catastrophe conditions.

answers.answer: Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 per existing Debt, per officer or regiment in an Army, and per ship in sea zones, including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans and advance Debt one per loan until the track ends, but continue receiving loans even at maximum Debt. Emergency Debt added this way creates no additional expense this turn. After using the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then check remaining Balance against expectations for the current Standing; if it is below expectations, lower Standing one. After that, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, each costing one cash per Company share and paying each owner £1 per share. If the total cash paid as dividends is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
answers.evidence: Revenue: Expenses, Expectations, Dividends list emergency-loan rules and the order of Standing checks.

answers.answer: An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary attacks in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order, with each Commander ordering attacks within their Presidency. A normal Crisis primary attack uses the normal attack calculation plus local unrest; for Foreign Invasion, use the ordinary attack die under the designer exception rather than adding unrest. A secondary attack’s strength is only that region’s unrest. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use their printed strength and cannot be split. If the newly exhausted defense strength is insufficient, the Company loses the region. If sufficient, clear all unrest there and the Commander takes one trophy. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts instead, or Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gains or loses no trophies. The summary also says a failed primary Invasion removes one tower from the attacker if possible, while a successful primary Invasion applies empire growth.
answers.evidence: Attacks on Company: secondary attacks follow primary, Presidency order, strength and defense-piece rules; successful defense clears unrest and awards a trophy; vacant-Commander fallback is specified.

answers.answer: The PM reveals up to three laws, chooses one, discards the others, chooses direction around the dial and stops at the first matching policy space; a dilemma forces selection and ends drawing. Voting begins with the PM and proceeds clockwise. A final support of -1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma’s If Failed text, transfer the PM dial to the Opposition Leader, and have the new PM move the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolve that adjacent policy. Support of zero or more passes, so zero passes: place the law among passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first, then the law’s immediate effects. After either outcome, restore all voting cards to their regular orientation. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament resolution: ‘-1 or less fails’; ‘Zero or higher passes’; failed vote changes PM and policy; passed vote resolves selected policy then immediate law effects.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. On passage, lower Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. This special vote has no policy, does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law on failure, and the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario begins deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: session timing and lined/starred trigger; pass and fail effects; no policy, PM retention, and 1813 exception.

answers.answer: To form a firm, a player not already managing a firm contributes an eligible Company share (returned to supply) or flips a workshop to its invested side. Flip the family board to a firm charter, place a family member as the first firm share, set the value cube to the track’s leftmost space, and take £5 from the bank into London treasury. With the manager’s consent, a player can invest another Company share or workshop in the same way to create one firm share and add £5 from the bank to London. The Chairman’s share cannot be used. Company shares cannot be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and shares created this turn cannot be used even if traded away. A firm can have up to ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no shares. An invested workshop never returns to uninvested status, gives no workshop bonus or Company-failure VP, and remains invested even if the firm fails.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Form and Invest: contribution, £5 bank funding, consent, Chairman/track restrictions, ten-share limit, and invested-workshop treatment.

answers.answer: Each manager secretly selects a sea zone/home port and a London cash bid, and must have at least one ship to select a zone; a closed home port is allowed. Alternatively, choose Hobnob with no bid: it does not trade or pay dividends but still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Reveal bids simultaneously while keeping strategies facedown until the associated Presidency begins. At that Presidency’s operations, before actions, matching firms reveal strategy and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 succeeds. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice; the President’s successful Trade creates initiative in the same way. Following the President’s Trade success, fill orders from lowest initiative upward. The President chooses the order among tied traders, with no automatic Company priority. If the President is vacant or does not successfully trade, firms fill after the Commander and Governors have had a chance; the Chairman breaks initiative ties. Each firm fills as many open orders as possible up to ships plus one, starting at its strategy home port and tracing its own filled route back there; it fills each particular order only once. It may refill orders filled earlier that turn by another firm or the Company, and the Company may refill firm-filled orders. Previously filled orders pay half listed revenue rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for each full £6 added to its India treasury that turn. There is only one trade attempt per firm per turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: strategy, bid check, initiative and tie timing; order-fill capacity/routes, repeat-filled revenue, and value growth.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, before Company revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of their share count or firm Value. They may use either or both treasuries. If unable to pay, the firm dissolves unless rescued. On dissolution, its shares go to Debtor’s Prison and each costs -1 VP, ships return to shipyards, and the charter returns to family side; invested workshops stay invested. Emergency investments follow the usual Company-share/workshop rules, even if the ten-share cap prevents new shares; they pay expenses, any remaining money is lost, and firm Value falls one space per emergency investment. Alternatively, the firm may merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends from India treasury only. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with manager consent, a shareholder may forgo payment on any number of their shares. Record the total actual cash paid out, rather than a per-share amount, with the dividend cube on the Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep remaining India funds into London treasury.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: expense formula and funding, dissolution outcomes, rescue choices, dividend calculation and treasury sweep.
